# Stronger retained baseline: certified forgetting, not a reduced recurrence

This separate falsification fixture does not modify the frozen reviewed
construction. A long-word-only timing comparison can favor a small recurrence
while overlooking an ordinary method that does almost no recurrence at all.

Let C_a be the same acquired stochastic center matrices and mu the task's
initial probability distribution. Choose the uniform distribution h as a
cheap proposal, and CHECK

    d=min_(a,i,j) C_a[i,j]/h_j,
    xi=max_a ||h^T C_a-h^T||_1.

No exact invariant law or common stationary distribution is asserted. For
d<1 write C_a=d*1*h^T+(1-d)R_a, with R_a stochastic. For any probability nu,

    ||nu^T C_a-h^T||_1
       <= (1-d)||nu-h||_1 + xi.

Indeed (nu-h)^T*1*h^T=0, stochastic R contracts row l1 norm, and h^T C-h^T is
the paid drift. At d=1 the kernel is the reset to h and xi=0. Thus the exact
recurrence D_0=||mu-h||_1, D_(t+1)=min(2,(1-d)D_t+xi) gives a uniform bound
for every sequence, even when the centers have no common equilibrium.

For the same entry boxes and eta_inf as in PROOF.md, a constant answer h^T b
has error at length l at most

    ||b||_infinity * (l*eta_inf + D_l),

plus its paid final scalar rounding. (Centering b can improve the constant;
this test deliberately uses the displayed conservative bound.) Whenever
this meets the tolerance, return the same constant for EVERY word of that
length, after reading/validating its symbols. For other lengths use ordinary
retained full-center integer replay with its existing infinity-norm budget.
The hybrid therefore admits every word of length <=L, not only the easy long
test words. It retains the observed center matrices for fallback; their
storage and any later compilation/application are not discarded from cost.

On the existing 12-state finite-observation fixture, this ordinary comparator
can answer every tested horizon-30 word with zero matrix-vector products.
The precise threshold, bounds and fallback work are in the executable report.
This erases the reduced-rank methods' online advantage for that long-word
batch, even before charging their acquisition. It does not disprove the
two-sided certificate or claim every family mixes rapidly. It identifies an
important strongest-baseline failure of this particular proposed advantage.

# Separate certified-forgetting comparator review

31 October 2026. Scoped mathematical and fixture-code PASS after full read:

- `MIXING_BASELINE.md`: SHA-256 `f610578cc1d8ee32c150d5e3d9c7dcfff534da5660c1edf913c2f26e4bdf122d`.
- `mixing_baseline.py`: `fd7e8eb15088068b2d349bbfae4ef5180276faa1f3705e3d95f44f23dc6b2918`.
- Frozen results: `mixing_baseline_results.json`, `9a73d4416d7c18a3740a1ecaf7c94c6fa30954adf7b05a5c7e041c76baf20366`.

The earlier imperfect-observation proof/code and its receipt are unchanged.

For stochastic C with C>=d*1*h^T, the difference of probability rows nu-h has zero total mass. Its reset term therefore vanishes, while stochastic R contracts row l1. Adding the checked drift h^T C-h^T proves the displayed affine recurrence. The independent probability-distance bound supplies the cap at 2. At d=1 the channel resets to h exactly and xi=0. No exact common invariant distribution is assumed.

Pairing with b gives ||b||_infinity D_l. Adding the already acquired stochastic-center observation transport gives ||b||_infinity(l eta_inf+D_l), and final scalar rounding is separately paid. Each length has its own checked rule; the code does not extrapolate the admitted interval to arbitrary longer words. Uniformity in every word permits the chronological/reverse observable convention used by the earlier replay API, since the entire set of words is bounded.

For fallback, initialization plus l rounded center applications contribute at most (l+1)q in infinity norm. Probability mu has l1 norm one; final output rounding adds q. Thus M*l*eta_inf+(l+2)q is a valid fallback bound. Both branches retain the same finite observations; center storage and any actual fallback compilation/products are not removed from the cost. This executable is a known-fixture comparator, not a newly hardened external verifier.

I independently reran the file in a separate temporary working directory. All 240 checks passed. The checked minorization is 9831/32768 and reference drift is 1/147456. Constant answering is admitted at every length from 16 through 30, while the shorter lengths use the paid full-center fallback. All 40 existing horizon-30 queries were answered with zero matrix-vector products and no fallback compilation. Symbol validation and reading the word still occur.
